title: Telemetry budget-aware sampling and onboarding guide
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes Redwood's recommended approach for onboarding enterprise customers to a budget-aware telemetry sampling strategy. It focuses on balancing fidelity and observability cost by combining adaptive sampling, reservoir sampling for high-cardinality tenants, and cost-feedback loops driven by billing/ingestion signals. The guide contains architecture patterns, configuration examples, rollout steps, acceptance criteria, and an operational runbook for support teams.

Goals
-----
- Ensure observable signal quality for SLOs and QBR metrics while controlling telemetry ingestion cost at tenant and org levels.
- Provide a reproducible onboarding checklist that Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Platform teams can follow.
- Reduce noise and storage costs without losing critical anomaly and regression signals.

When to use this guide
----------------------
Use this playbook for new enterprise tenants where expected telemetry volume or cost could exceed baseline thresholds, or for existing customers whose telemetry spend triggers a cost-protection review. Typical triggers:
- Projected ingestion > $2k/month for logs/metrics/traces (estimate)
- Hosting dedicated or high-throughput agents behind heavy API traffic
- Customers requesting strict cost caps or billing alerts

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1) Data sources: SDKs, agent-side sampling, edge sidecars, ingress proxies.
2) Adaptive sampling service: centralized orchestration that issues per-tenant sampling policies and receives cost/traffic telemetry.
3) Store & query: short-term hot store + long-term cold store; sampling tags preserved for deterministic rehydration.
4) Cost telemetry & feedback: ingestion meter emits cost estimates back to the adaptive sampling service for policy updates.

Core concepts and patterns
--------------------------
- Budget-aware sampling: set a target ingestion budget and tune sampling to meet it while prioritizing high-value traces/events.
- Priority buckets: classify events/traces into priority tiers (critical, high, normal, debug) using rules derived from tenant-provided signal sets.
- Reservoir sampling for high-cardinality keys: maintain a fixed reservoir per key (user_id/session_id) to avoid missing rare but important patterns.
- Deterministic retention tags: attach deterministic tags so downstream ingestion can rehydrate or re-evaluate samples if needed.
- Grace windows: when a model rollout or canary is active, temporarily raise fidelity for affected traffic slices.

Sampling algorithms we recommend
------------------------------
- Static-rate sampling: simple global rate for low-risk tenants. Good as a baseline.
- Adaptive latency-aware sampling: increase sampling for requests with latency > p95 to keep tail behavior visible.
- Budget-driven proportional sampling: compute per-minute budget deficit and multiply base sampling by budget_factor = target_spend/current_spend.
- Hybrid reservoir+probabilistic: reservoir for cardinality keys + probabilistic sampling for generic events.

Configuration examples
----------------------
Below is a representative YAML policy that the adaptive sampling service consumes. Replace variables as appropriate for the tenant.

# Example: tenant sampling policy
tenant_id: tenant-1234
budget_monthly_usd: 1200
priority_buckets:
  critical:
    selectors:
      - event.type == \"deployment_error\"
    sample_rate: 1.0
  high:
    selectors:
      - request.latency_ms > 500
    sample_rate: 0.75
  normal:
    selectors: []
    sample_rate: 0.2
  debug:
    selectors: []
    sample_rate: 0.02
reservoir_keys:
  - user_id
  - session_id
reservoir_target_per_minute: 1000
budget_mode: proportional
budget_evaluation_window_minutes: 60

CLI and API snippets
--------------------
- Inspect current policy: redwoodctl sampling get --tenant tenant-1234
- Apply policy: redwoodctl sampling apply --file tenant-1234-sampling.yaml
- Force snapshot of reservoir state: redwoodctl sampling snapshot --tenant tenant-1234 --out /tmp/snap.json

Rollout and onboarding steps (owner assignments)
------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-onboard (Solutions Eng)
   - Collect expected QPS, user cardinality, peak window and cost constraints from customer. (Owner: Solutions Eng)
   - Baseline: deploy instrumentation agent on staging and collect 72 hours of data. (Owner: Customer Success + SE)
2) Policy design (Customer Success + Eng Platform)
   - Create initial policy YAML using templates above. (Owner: Eng Platform)
   - Decide priority buckets and reservoir keys with customer. (Owner: Customer Success)
3) Staging validation (Customer Success + Customer)
   - Apply policy to staging, run synthetic traffic for 24-48 hours. Validate that SLO telemetry remains visible (p50/p95/p99). (Owner: Customer Success)\   - Generate cost estimate report for the month given observed ingest rates. (Owner: Finance-legal telemetry)
4) Canary (Eng SRE + Customer)
   - Canary to 5–10% production traffic slice or to a small service subset. Monitor signal fidelity and missed-anomaly rate. (Owner: Eng SRE)
5) Full rollout and tune (Customer Success + Eng SRE)
   - Gradually increase to 100% over 24–72 hours with close monitoring. Tune bucket rates and reservoir targets. (Owner: Customer Success)

Acceptance criteria and QBR signals
----------------------------------
- Telemetry cost at or below target budget ±10% after first full calendar month.
- No more than 2 missed P0 anomalies during the first 30 days attributable to sampling.
- SLO visibility: key SLI time-series (error rate, p95 latency, tokens-per-request) retain >= 95% of pre-sampling alert fidelity for critical services.
- QBR metrics to track: ingestion_cost_by_tenant, sampling_rate_by_bucket, missed_anomaly_count, reservoir_fill_ratio

Monitoring dashboards and alerts
------------------------------
Create the following dashboards before canary:
- Tenant overview: total ingestion per hour, cost estimate rolling 30d, sampling rate heatmap.
- Bucket fidelity: per-bucket event counts, anomaly detection hit-rate, representative examples.
- Reservoir health: fill ratio, eviction rate, top keys by cardinality.

Suggested alerts (examples)
- ingestion_cost_estimate > budget_monthly_usd * 1.15 (SEV-3)
- missed_anomaly_count > 1 in 24 hours (SEV-2)
- reservoir_fill_ratio < 0.5 for 30 minutes (SEV-2)

Operational runbook (support process)
------------------------------------
1) Customer reports increased cost or missing signals.
2) Triage owner (Customer Success) opens a joint incident channel and collects: tenant_id, sampling policy version, example event IDs, and timeframe.
3) Quick checks (Eng SRE)
   - Verify policy is applied: redwoodctl sampling get --tenant <id>
   - Check ingestion spike sources: ingress proxy logs and SDK agent versions.
   - Correlate ingest rate vs. billing meter for last 24h.
4) If fidelity issue confirmed, options: temporarily raise sampling for affected selectors, deploy a grace window, or snapshot and backfill high-priority traces to cold store for targeted windows.
5) Post-incident: adjust policy and add guardrail alerts to prevent recurrence.

Troubleshooting matrix
----------------------
- Symptom: sudden drop in p95 visibility
  - Likely cause: overly aggressive global rate; stale reservoir keys
  - Action: roll back to previous policy, increase normal bucket to 0.5, start a canary.
- Symptom: ingestion cost unexpectedly high
  - Likely cause: misconfigured selectors or policy not applied (agent mismatch)
  - Action: confirm agent version and policy hash; revert to earlier policy; throttle agent sidecar.
- Symptom: reservoir starvation for a key
  - Likely cause: incorrect key selection or hot-key anomaly
  - Action: temporarily promote key to high priority and increase reservoir_target_per_minute

Customer-facing communication templates
--------------------------------------
- Initial onboarding note: a one-paragraph summary of the expected behavior, staging dates, and cost guardrails.
- Incident advisory: brief description, immediate mitigation steps, timeline for root cause analysis, and next steps.

Appendix: checklist (quick)
--------------------------
- [ ] Collect traffic profile (QPS, peak QPS, cardinality)
- [ ] Baseline 72h staging data collected
- [ ] Initial policy created and reviewed
- [ ] Dashboards provisioned and alerts created
- [ ] Canary executed and acceptance criteria met
- [ ] Full rollout and cost validation completed

Appendix: useful links
----------------------
- Sampling policy templates: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/sampling-templates
- redwoodctl reference: https://internal.redwood.dev/tools/redwoodctl#sampling
- Cost attribution docs: /confluence/finance-and-legal/billing/ingest-cost-attribution

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary contact: Customer Success Manager (owner per tenant)
- Platform steward: Eng Platform (sampling service)
- SRE on-call: first responder for canary and production incidents
- Escalation path: Customer Success -> Eng Platform -> Security (if data integrity concerns) -> VP Customer Success
